status: frozen before any C1 result (REVEALS downloaded and its column header read; no values inspected)
question: Does AD 200 forest = potential forest x (1 - cleared share), with clearing driven by the population model's density (Kaplan, Krumhardt & Zimmermann 2009: clearing rises with people, per-capita land use falling), reproduce the pollen-based open-land share of Europe at the start of the era?
target: REVEALS open land (OL, % of the 1-degree cell) in time window TW6 = 2.2-1.7 ka BP (c. 250 BCE - 250 CE), Fyfe et al. 2021, PANGAEA doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.937075 (CC BY 4.0; Githumbi et al. 2022, ESSD 14, 1581); cells inside the Earth run (output/land_people/earth/earth.npz: 0-56 N, 12 W-125 E) with >= 30 % land

model.potential: the map's forest share by Whittaker biome (harvest.models.FOREST_SHARE: savanna 0.5, forest biomes 1.0, others 0) on the Earth run's climate; not fitted
model.density: the population model on Earth: settlement base x central occupation x old-core term (cradles + Rome, travel cost, L 800 km; reports/POPULATION_20261023.md), renormalized to the base's total over land (as harvest/export settlement_cored)
model.clearing: c(P) = 1 - exp(-(P / P0)^k); open share of a cell = mean over its land of 1 - f0 x (1 - c)
model.fit: P0 in a log grid 1-300 people/km2, k in {0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2}; minimum RMSE on the development cells

split: 5-degree blocks in a checkerboard: block = floor((lat - 30) / 5) + floor((lon + 25) / 5); even blocks development, odd blocks blind

baselines.B1: one constant cleared share, fitted on the development cells

blind_gates.G1: candidate RMSE below both B0 and B1 on the blind cells
blind_gates.G2: candidate Spearman rank correlation above B1's on the blind cells
blind_gates.adopt: both: the map's forest share at AD 200 = potential x (1 - c(P)) with the map's own population density, and C2 (forest share in travel cost and control) is tested next on Earth; else the clearing rule is revised

amendment_1.status: after the first development fit, before any blind cell was read
amendment_1.finding: The biome potential is broken for Europe: 75 % of central and western European Earth-run land (median 8.8 C, 687 mm) falls in Whittaker woodland/shrubland (forest share 0), so even with no clearing the model predicts 0.75 open land against 0.42 observed on the development cells (Spearman ~0); the fit runs to the grid edge (P0 300, k 0.5). Whittaker envelopes ignore evaporation; at low PET 700 mm carries deciduous forest.
amendment_1.change: potential forest f0 = clip((AI - a) / w, 0, 1) x clip((GDD5 - g0) / 300, 0, 1), AI = P_ann / PET_ann and GDD5 from the Earth run (the map computes both); a in {0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7}, w in {0.2, 0.4, 0.8}, g0 in {300, 600}, fitted jointly with the clearing curve on the development blocks. B0 and B1 use the same fitted potential (the potential is fitted for each baseline too), so the gates still test whether population-driven clearing adds skill. The biome potential is reported.
